units.title: Covariance, correlation & regression
units.description: See how two quantities move together, then build a line that describes their relationship.

units.title: Foundations of probability & counting
units.description: Start with outcomes and events. Build probability rules, permutations, combinations, and careful counting.

units.title: Conditional probability, independence & Bayes
units.description: Change the reference group, follow probability paths, and use evidence to update a probability.

units.title: Random variables, expectation & variance
units.description: Turn outcomes into numbers. Connect probability masses to averages, spread, transformations, and sums.

units.title: Counting models
units.description: One Bernoulli trial leads to binomial, hypergeometric, and Poisson counts. Compare assumptions, probabilities, means, and variances.

units.title: Formula and concept review
units.description: Connect data summaries, probability, conditioning, and discrete models with course notation, formulas, and click-controlled diagrams.

units.title: Continuous random variables & the normal distribution
units.description: Move from probability mass to density and area. Explore cumulative probability, uniform and normal distributions, standardization, and percentiles.

links.label: CLT notes, group practice & worked solutions · 4 pages

units.title: Confidence intervals
units.description: Build confidence intervals for means and proportions, interpret confidence and precision, and plan sample sizes. Follow the notes in class order and try three practice problems.

links.label: Student notes & practice · 18 pages · no solutions

videos.title: Bayes theorem, the geometry of changing beliefs
videos.description: An area picture for changing the reference group and updating beliefs.

videos.title: The medical test paradox, and redesigning Bayes’ rule
videos.description: A diagnostic-testing example that makes the role of the base rate visible.

videos.title: Binomial distributions | Probabilities of probabilities, part 1
videos.description: A visual companion to repeated trials and binomial counts. The later inference material is optional.

videos.title: The quick proof of Bayes’ theorem
videos.description: A short Bayes proof with a discussion of independence.

videos.title: But what is the Central Limit Theorem?
videos.description: Further intuition for the normal distribution and the Central Limit Theorem. You do not need to know the binomial-to-normal approximation formulas.

recorded_lectures.title: A confidence interval for the usable-sample rate
recorded_lectures.description: Work through the usable-kit proportion, its standard error, the 95% confidence interval, and a careful interpretation. The walkthrough ends after part (a).

recorded_lectures.title: Hypotheses, p-values, and significance
recorded_lectures.description: Build a null reference model, calculate one- and two-sided p-values, and use the GPA example to make a significance decision.
recorded_lectures.endpoint: Covered through original slide 20, “Significance level,” including the qualitative p-value evidence bands. We resume at slide 21, “Significance level & critical values.”
